body.p: Immense numbers (several thousands) of these Pardons have been passed upon favorably; the Pardon Warrants, (like great deeds) have been issued from the State Department, on the requisition of this office. But for some reason or other, they nearly all yet lie awaiting the President's signature. He seems to be in no hurry about it, but lets them wait.

The crowds that come here are greet make a curious study for me. I get along, very sociably, however when talking with any of them,—as I let them do all the talking; only now & then I g ask a suggestive question or two.

If the thing continues as at present, all the property‸& wealthof the Southern States is going to‸legally rest, for the future, on these pardons. Every single one is made out with the condition that they the grantee shall respect the abolition of slavery & never make an attempt to restore it.
